text:
Alex H: Pager fired: autoscaler in us-west hit repeated eviction cycles, causing 503s for inference routes. Paging oncall.
SRE-Bot: INCIDENT | Pager: autoscaler-evictions-us-west at 2025-11-12T15:12:25Z
Maya R: seeing 503 spikes on /v1/generate from eu-west and us-west? looks like us-west is origin; traffic shift triggered autoscaler churn.
Javier S: I've got the bridge up: <https://call.link/bridge123>
Liz P: tagging product/solutions to track customer impact. Which customers affected?
Maya R: internal metrics show about 12 orgs with >5% error rate in last 10m; top affected: Acme, Quokka, Brightly
Alex H: immediate mitigation: scale reservations for gn4-pool-2 by +2 and pin critical orgs to dedicated nodes. Doing `kubectl scale ...` now.
Javier S: command run:
```
kubectl annotate hpa/autoscaler-us-west rti/disable-scale=false
kubectl patch deployment gn4-inference --patch '{"spec":{"replicas":10}}'
```
Oncall: rolling back the recent autoscaler config change (temp) — deploying canary rollback.
Maya R: note: rollback will reduce burst capacity; prefer to add temporary reservations first.
SRE-Bot: ALERT | Rollback deployed by @Oncall at 2025-11-12T15:22:40Z
Alex H: rollback completed. Observability: 503s dropped to baseline over 4m but latency increased slightly for small seqs.
Liz P: product: we'll notify affected customers. Draft notice in #customer-comms: "We experienced degraded inference availability in us-west..." — will post once we have root cause.
Maya R: root cause preliminary: a config drift in autoscaler target RPS thresholds combined with a GPU eviction wave on gn4 pool — likely underlying spot preemptions in region, HF.
Javier S: logs excerpt:
```
[15:12:10] eviction: node-gn4-23 preempted by provider
[15:12:11] pod gn4-inference-abc evicted: Preemption
[15:12:12] scaler: target_rps=800 current_rps=1100 => scale_up triggered
```
Alex H: action items (assign owners):
- INF-4321: Add temporary capacity buffer to us-west autoscaler config (+20% headroom) -> owner: Javier S
- INF-4322: Investigate node preemption pattern (provider-side) -> owner: Maya R
- INF-4323: Create dedicated reservation flow for high-SLA customers -> owner: Liz P
- INF-4324: Postmortem + publish timeline -> owner: Alex H
Oncall: creating Jira tickets now, linking this thread.
SRE-Bot: JIRA | Created INF-4321, INF-4322, INF-4323, INF-4324
Maya R: scheduling 30m postmortem sync tomorrow 0900 PT. Calendar invite sent to SRE, Eng-Infra, Product.
Liz P: customer impact estimate: 12 customers, peak error rate 18% for 7 minutes; revenue-sensitive customers: Acme and Brightly. I'll draft outbound w/ support.
Alex H: temporary mitigations checklist:
- pinned 2 critical orgs to reserved nodes (done)
- bumped pod disruption budget (in progress)
- toggled eviction-sensitive taints on nodes for a short window
Javier S: ETA for INF-4321 rollout = 2h (testing + canary). Will update thread when merged.
Oncall: final notes: no data loss, API errors were 5xx, not 4xx; customers may have retried. Flagging for SLA credit review.
Liz P: opening support tickets for top-affected customers and syncing with CSMs.
Alex H: postmortem owner assigned INF-4324; I'll own timeline and draft. Expect publish in 3 business days after infra analysis.
Maya R: follow-ups: add an SLO guardrail that prevents autoscaler from oscillating when >n preemptions detected. New ticket INF-4330.
SRE-Bot: REMINDER | Postmortem meeting tomorrow 2025-11-13T09:00:00-08:00 (link in calendar)
Alex H: thanks everyone. Keeping thread open for status updates; tag me for escalations. :pray:
